clue.text: Very effective at the outset to block Conservative over worker's contract

indicators.note: something that blocks sits inside a passage, so these letters go inside the party word

parts.note: CON is the usual short form of Conservative

indicators.note: the outset of a word is its opening letter, so only the leading letters of the two words count

parts.note: opening letters of the two words
a worker ant; the 's attaches it to the contract

explanation.surface: A tough union deal: the Tories muscling in on a working man's employment contract.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places CON(VE)N above ANT, giving COVENANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding agreement, a solemn kind of contract.

explanation.walkthrough: Take the T out of METRE to leave MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere is an old and poetic word for a lake or pond, still found in English place names.

explanation.definitionFit: Orange is the name of a European royal dynasty, the House of Orange-Nassau of the Netherlands.
